analysis:
Examined the head text of .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (lines 1-1157) and the three changelog.d files. The workflow now builds once per lane (build-cluster, build-provider) and uploads the products via the local ./.github/actions/provider-ci-products action. Test jobs download them and run with --skip-build. A new cluster-release-checks job is added, the cluster shards grow to 3, and a resource sampler is added.

Security-relevant observations:
- Permissions stay at contents: read. Checkouts keep persist-credentials: false. Third-party actions remain SHA-pinned. The two actions/cache restore/save steps for MiMo audio (lines 453, 464) have no version comment but are pinned to the same SHA.
- Caches are saved only on push to master or dev (SAVE_CACHES). Pull requests restore caches and save none, which limits cache poisoning from PR code. Cluster release build cache keys bind the toolchain, manifests and submodule pins.
- The test-products hand-off crosses job boundaries through artifacts. Its integrity and commit/toolchain checks live in the unchanged-in-this-batch composite action and scripts/ci-test-products.py, which were not supplied. The changelog claims test jobs refuse products from another commit or toolchain. I could not verify this, so it is a coverage limit rather than a finding.
- Runner selection depends on the routes input. Darkbloom Sandbox runner grants and the route job (provider-plan.yml) were not supplied, so I could not check runner trust and label qualification.
- The resource-sample artifacts and coverage artifacts contain only process and memory metrics, with 14-day retention.
- Nothing here touches provider runtime code, the coordinator-provider wire, the attestation chain or the prefix cache (T-041). The changelog's hash-bundle memory change refers to provider source not supplied here.

No concrete regressions against the threat model were identified. Integration questions: the artifact provenance checks in provider-ci-products and the route/runner label handling in provider-plan.yml.
